items.title: NASA completes Artemis II rehearsal, clearing path for moon launch

featured_image.name: Artemis 2 SLS wet dress rehearsal latest news: 'Launch ...

items.description:
NASA wrapped up a successful wet dress rehearsal for the Artemis II mission on Wednesday night, clearing a major hurdle in the agency's push to send astronauts around the moon for the first time in more than 50 years. The rehearsal concluded at 10:16 p.m. EST on February 19, ending as planned at T-29 seconds in the simulated countdown.[1][2][3]

The test marked a turnaround from a troubled first attempt earlier this month. During the initial wet dress rehearsal on February 2, a liquid hydrogen leak at the base of the Space Launch System rocket forced NASA to cut the countdown short at the T-5 minute, 15-second mark, prompting the agency to wave off its February launch window entirely.[4][5]

items.title: World leaders set to issue joint AI stance at India summit

featured_image.name: Modi positions India as AI leader at India AI Impact Summit ...

items.description:
Dozens of world leaders, tech executives, and policymakers gathered in New Delhi this week for the India AI Impact Summit 2026, the largest global AI summit to date and the first held in a developing nation. As the five-day event at Bharat Mandapam nears its close, participants are expected to deliver a joint declaration on Friday outlining a shared approach to managing artificial intelligence.[1][2]

The summit — the fourth in an annual series following gatherings in the United Kingdom, South Korea, and France — drew more than 20 heads of state, over 100 country delegations, and tens of thousands of attendees from across the AI industry.[3][4][5]

items.title: NASA says 15,000 'city-killer' asteroids remain untracked with no defense ready

featured_image.name: "It Keeps Me up at Night": NASA Warns Earth Is Threatened by 15,000 Asteroids Big Enough to Wipe Out a City

items.description:
Roughly 15,000 asteroids large enough to obliterate a city are orbiting near Earth undetected, and humanity has no spacecraft ready to deflect any of them. That was the blunt assessment delivered this week by NASA officials at the American Association for the Advancement of Science annual meeting in Phoenix, Arizona.

Dr. Kelly Fast, NASA's acting planetary defense officer, told conference attendees that scientists have identified an estimated 25,000 asteroids measuring at least 140 meters in diameter — large enough to cause catastrophic regional destruction — but current detection systems have catalogued only about 40 percent of them. "What keeps me up at night are the asteroids we don't know about," Fast said, according to the Washington Times. "It's the ones in between that could do regional damage".[1][2][3]

items.title: Venezuela passes amnesty bill for political prisoners

featured_image.name: Venezuela passes amnesty bill for political prisoners in first of two votes

items.description:
Venezuela's National Assembly on Thursday approved an amnesty bill that could lead to the release of politicians, activists, lawyers, and many others detained for political reasons, according to the Associated Press. The measure, which passed unanimously after two weeks of negotiations, effectively acknowledges that the government has held hundreds of people in prison for political motivations — a stark reversal for a country whose authorities denied the existence of political prisoners for decades.[1][2]

Acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who proposed the legislation in late January under pressure from the Trump administration following the U.S. military capture of Nicolás Maduro on January 3, is expected to sign the bill into law.[3][2]

items.title: Iran warns UN that Trump remarks raise risk of conflict

featured_image.name: Iran urges UN to respond to Trump's ‘reckless' threats over protests

items.description:
Iran has declared in a letter to UN Secretary-General António Guterres that President Donald Trump's recent rhetoric signals "a real risk of military aggression" and warned that Tehran will target the bases, facilities, and assets of any hostile force if it faces an attack, according to Iran's permanent mission to the United Nations.[1][2]

The letter, sent Thursday, emphasized that while Iran does not seek war, any military aggression would be met with a decisive response. Iran's warning follows Trump's announcement at the inaugural meeting of his Board of Peace that Tehran has approximately 10 days to reach a deal with Washington or face potential military strikes.[3][2][4][1]

items.title: Italy considers adding 100,000 military personnel by 2044

featured_image.name: Italy considers adding 100,000 personnel to armed forces ...

items.description:
Italy's defense ministry is weighing a sweeping proposal to increase military personnel by more than 60 percent over the next 18 years, according to a document seen by Reuters. The plan, presented this week to Defence Minister Guido Crosetto, would grow the combined strength of the army, navy, and air force from approximately 170,000 to 275,000 personnel, including a 15,000-strong reserve, at an estimated cost of around six billion euros.[1][2]

The proposal, drafted by military experts, lays the groundwork for an ambitious overhaul of the Italian armed forces that officials expect to unveil by the end of March. If implemented, personnel costs would rise to nearly 15 billion euros from the current 8.8 billion euros, with the expansion phased in gradually through 2044.[2][1]

items.title: North Korea opens 9th Party Congress with Kim claiming economic success

featured_image.name: North Korea to convene 9th Congress in late February, KCNA ...

items.description:
North Korea convened its Ninth Party Congress on Thursday, the country's largest political gathering held every five years, according to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).[1][2]

In his opening speech, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared that the economy had overcome recession and the country accomplished major economic goals over the past five years, KCNA reported. The claim marks a striking contrast to the 8th Party Congress in January 2021, when Kim acknowledged that his previous five-year economic plan had failed "in almost all sectors."[3][4][2][1]

items.title: Former Prince Andrew released after arrest in Epstein-related probe

featured_image.name: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor officially stripped of two more titles

items.description:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former Prince Andrew, was released by British police late Thursday after being held for approximately 11 hours following his arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office, Thames Valley Police confirmed.[1][2]

The arrest, which occurred on Mountbatten-Windsor's 66th birthday at Wood Farm on King Charles III's Sandringham estate in Norfolk, marks the first time the former royal has been detained by police. He departed a police station in a black Range Rover Thursday evening after being released "under investigation," meaning he has neither been charged nor exonerated.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: World Bank opens Gaza reconstruction fund as nations pledge $17B

featured_image.name: Trump hosts inaugural meeting of his Board of Peace ...

items.description:
World Bank President Ajay Banga announced Thursday that the Gaza Reconstruction and Development Fund is now ready to accept donations, marking a step toward rebuilding the war-devastated Palestinian territory as nations pledge billions at the first meeting of President Donald Trump's Board of Peace in Washington.

Banga, speaking at the inaugural gathering at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace, said the fund would secure donor money while the Board of Peace directs disbursements for reconstruction and development projects in the Gaza Strip. He assured donors that "robust financial, legal and oversight mechanisms" are in place to guarantee transparency about how the money is utilized.[1][2]

"The World Bank's role is that of a limited trustee," Banga explained, according to Middle East Eye. "Because of our AAA rating, we have the ability to leverage private bond money to help to create the resources we need... we can de-risk private investing."[2]

items.title: US gives IEA one year to drop net zero agenda or face withdrawal

featured_image.name: US renews threat to leave IEA

items.description:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright issued a stark ultimatum to the International Energy Agency at its ministerial meeting in Paris this week, demanding the organization abandon its net-zero emissions agenda within a year or face American withdrawal.

Speaking at the conclusion of the two-day ministerial gathering on Thursday, Wright told reporters that the US would "exert all the pressure we have" to push the IEA away from its climate-focused agenda, calling net zero a "destructive illusion" with a "zero percent chance" of being realized.[1][2]

items.title: Trump gives Iran 10 days to reach nuclear deal or face action

featured_image.name: Trump touts peace while threatening war with Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that the United States will determine within approximately 10 days whether to pursue military action against Iran or continue with diplomatic negotiations over Tehran's nuclear program, issuing his most direct ultimatum yet in a crisis that has seen the largest American military buildup in the Middle East since 2003.

"Good talks are being had. It's proven to be, over the years, not easy to make a meaningful deal with Iran. We have to make a meaningful deal, otherwise bad things happen," Trump said during the first meeting of his Board of Peace in Washington. "So now we may have to take a step further or may not. Maybe we're going to make a deal. You're going to be finding out over the next, probably, 10 days."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Ukraine drone barrage ignites Russian oil depot after Geneva talks collapse

featured_image.name: Russia downs 113 Ukrainian drones as refinery comes under ...

items.description:
Russian air defense forces intercepted 113 Ukrainian drones overnight on February 18-19, the Russian Defense Ministry reported Thursday, in one of the largest drone assaults targeting Russian territory in recent weeks. The strikes came hours after U.S.-brokered peace talks in Geneva concluded without a breakthrough.

The heaviest concentration of drone activity targeted Russia's western border regions. According to the Defense Ministry, at least 50 drones were shot down over Bryansk Oblast, 35 over Smolensk Oblast, 12 over Tver Oblast, 10 over Novgorod Oblast, four over Leningrad Oblast, and two over Kaluga Oblast.[1]

items.title: UN probe says RSF siege of El-Fasher bears 'hallmarks of genocide'

featured_image.name: UN mission finds RSF destruction in el-Fasher bears ‘hallmarks of genocide'

items.description:
The United Nations' independent fact-finding mission on Sudan concluded Thursday that the Rapid Support Forces' siege and capture of El-Fasher last October bears "the hallmarks of genocide" against non-Arab communities, particularly the Zaghawa and Fur ethnic groups.[1][2]

The report documents a coordinated campaign of destruction following an 18-month siege that deliberately starved the city's population. RSF fighters killed more than 6,000 people between October 25 and 27, 2025, according to the UN Human Rights Office, in what investigators described as "three days of absolute horror".[3][4]

items.title: Five nations commit troops to Gaza security force, commander says

featured_image.name: Gaza's ISF commander was key in Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire | The Jerusalem Post

items.description:
Five nations formally committed military personnel to the International Stabilization Force for Gaza during the inaugural Board of Peace meeting on Thursday, marking a step forward for President Donald Trump's post-war reconstruction plan for the territory.

Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, and Albania pledged troops to the ISF, while Egypt and Jordan committed to training Palestinian police, according to ISF commander Major General Jasper Jeffers, who made the announcement at the meeting in Washington.[1][2][3]

The force will begin deploying in southern Gaza's Rafah and "expand sector by sector," Jeffers said. The long-term plan envisions 20,000 ISF troops supporting the transition of security responsibilities in the enclave as Israeli forces withdraw.[2][4]

items.title: US commits $10 billion to Trump’s Board of Peace

featured_image.name: Trump's Board of Peace pledges $5 billion for Gaza

items.description:
President Donald Trump convened the inaugural meeting of his Board of Peace on Thursday, announcing approximately $17 billion in total pledges for humanitarian and reconstruction efforts in war-torn Gaza. The announcement came at the U.S. Institute of Peace in Washington, where representatives from more than two dozen countries gathered to formalize commitments to the controversial initiative.[1][2][3]

Trump said the United States will contribute $10 billion to the Board of Peace, the international body he chairs under a mandate approved by the United Nations Security Council in November 2025. Nine countries — Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, the United Arab Emirates, Morocco, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan, and Kuwait — collectively pledged more than $7 billion, according to AFP and Associated Press reports. Trump also announced that the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs is raising an additional $2 billion, and that Japan has committed to hosting a fundraiser.[2][4][1]

items.title: Scientists first directly measure upper-atmosphere pollution from SpaceX rocket reentry

featured_image.name: SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets are grounded after inflight break up

items.description:
For the first time, researchers have directly measured pollution in Earth's upper atmosphere from a specific piece of space debris, tracing a plume of lithium vapor back to the uncontrolled reentry of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket over Europe last year.

The findings, published Thursday in the journal Communications Earth & Environment, mark a milestone in understanding how the burgeoning commercial space industry may be altering atmospheric chemistry in ways scientists are only beginning to comprehend.[1][2]

items.title: US deploys largest Middle East air force since 2003 Iraq invasion

featured_image.name: F-35s Deploy Closer to Middle East After US Talks with Iran

items.description:
The United States is assembling the largest concentration of military air power in the Middle East since the 2003 invasion of Iraq, positioning dozens of advanced fighter jets and a second aircraft carrier to the region as President Donald Trump weighs potential strikes on Iran.

According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, the U.S. Air Force has moved F-35s, F-22 Raptors, F-15Es, and F-16s to Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan and Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia in recent days, based on flight-tracking data. Command-and-control aircraft essential for large air campaigns, including E-3 Airborne Warning and Control System and E-11 Battlefield Airborne Communications Node aircraft, are also inbound.[1][2][3]

items.title: Climate change adding 47 extra days of harmful heat in coffee regions

featured_image.name: What climate change means for the future of coffee, cashews ...

items.description:
The world's leading coffee-producing regions are facing an average of 47 additional days of harmful heat annually due to climate change, threatening global harvests and contributing to elevated consumer prices, according to a new analysis released Wednesday by Climate Central.[1][2]

The study examined daily temperatures from 2021 to 2025 across 25 countries that represent 97% of global coffee production. Every country analyzed experienced more coffee-harming heat than would have occurred without fossil fuel pollution.[2][1]

items.title: South Korea's ex-president Yoon sentenced to life for insurrection

featured_image.name: South Korea's former President Yoon sentenced to five years: What we know

items.description:
Former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol was sentenced to life in prison on Thursday after a court found him guilty of leading an insurrection through his ill-fated declaration of martial law in December 2024, ending one of the most dramatic political crises in the country's democratic history.

Presiding Judge Ji Gwi-yeon of the Seoul Central District Court ruled that Yoon "directly and proactively planned" the insurrection and acted "with the purpose of subverting the Constitution by sending the military to the National Assembly to paralyze or limit its function for a substantial amount of time." Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that Yoon bore primary responsibility for destabilizing the constitutional order and had shown no remorse.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump convenes Board of Peace as Gaza disarmament stalls

featured_image.name: Trump convenes first 'Board of Peace' meeting as Gaza ...

items.description:
US President Donald Trump presided over the first meeting of his Board of Peace on Thursday, convening representatives from more than 45 nations in Washington to discuss the reconstruction of Gaza and the deployment of an international peacekeeping force. The meeting, held at the renamed Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace, comes as the Israel-Hamas ceasefire remains fragile and the central challenge of disarming Hamas unresolved.[1][2]

Trump announced this week that participating nations have pledged $5 billion for humanitarian relief and reconstruction efforts in Gaza, alongside commitments to deploy thousands of personnel to an International Stabilization Force aimed at maintaining security as Israeli forces withdraw from the territory.[3][4][5]
